result: In the LIFE-Long-COVID study (410 PCS, 87 recovered, 64 healthy), PCS showed worse episodic memory (b=-1.07) and visuospatial ability (b=-3.92) but no deficit in executive function, verbal fluency or global cognition; recovered infection without PCS showed no impairment.
reason: long COVID population with partly different domains (memory deficit overlaps, executive function spared); long COVID version, not an ME/CFS replication

result: Meta-analysis of 40 studies (6241 COVID survivors >3 months post-infection) found impaired 6MWT, VO2max and anaerobic threshold vs non-COVID controls, with similar resting VO2 and no differences in SpO2, heart rate, blood pressure, fatigue or dyspnoea during testing.
reason: same measure and direction but population is all COVID survivors vs uninfected controls rather than long COVID vs recovered controls; adds AT/6MWT pooling

result: Total IgG from long COVID patients stratified by GFAP and type-I interferon into 3 subgroups transferred persistent sensory hypersensitivity (2 subgroups) or reduced locomotor activity without motor incoordination (muscle-proteome subgroup) to mice.

result: In 54 acute COVID-19 patients, acute-phase IL-1RA, IFN-gamma, TNF-alpha and monocyte percentage predicted physical and total fatigue 6-9 months later, and higher acute TNF-alpha correlated with less awareness of cognitive fatigue (r=-0.40, p=.019).
reason: same mechanism (acute cytokine response predicting later fatigue) in a long COVID setting; small, fatigue scores not CFS case status, so extends rather than replicates

result: Acute COVID-19 IL-1RA, IFN-gamma, TNF-alpha and monocyte levels predicted fatigue 6-9 months later in 54 patients.

result: In 40 Gulf War Illness veterans, a randomised crossover of seated rest vs light, moderate and vigorous 20-min cycling showed no condition-by-time interaction for symptoms, pain sensitivity, cognition or most inflammatory markers within 1 h, and no effect on actigraphy over 7 days.
reason: Gulf War Illness population, not long COVID or ME/CFS, and not selected for PEM; no atlas finding covers GWI

result: In 40 GWI veterans, exercise at any intensity did not increase symptoms within 1 h or reduce activity over the following week relative to seated rest.
reason: does not measure PEM onset delay or recovery duration in ME/CFS; GWI population with outcomes only at 1 h
